prompt: Promotions do not all last two weeks, so compare each one with a baseline of its own length. For each promotion that started in 2025 (start_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025), give its length in days, the units sold on promotion, and the units of its products in the baseline. A sales line is on a promotion when it carries that promotion's ID in order_lines.promo_id, whatever its date; where two promotions overlap on a product, a line carries only the deeper one, so it counts once. The baseline ends the day before the promotion's start_date and has as many days as the promotion ran, start_date and end_date both counted; it holds every sales line of the promotion's products in those days, whatever promotion the line carries. Days are sales.order_date, the UTC day of the order. A promotion with no sale in a period shows 0 for it. Return four columns, in this order: promo_id, days, promo_units and baseline_units. Return one row for each such promotion. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per promotion that started in 2025

hints: Next, write the baseline window from the promotion's own length.
start_date minus order_date counts the days before the start: keep the lines where it runs from 1 up to the promotion's length.
faded_shape:
WITH promo AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT promo_id, start_date, end_date - start_date + 1 AS days
  FROM promotions
  WHERE start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
), during AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
  FROM promo p
  JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.promo_id = p.promo_id
  GROUP BY p.promo_id
), baseline AS (
  -- one row per promotion with a baseline sale
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(s.units) AS units
  FROM promo p
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = pp.product_id
why_this_works: Each baseline has its promotion's own number of days and ends just before it starts, so the two periods compare like with like.
faded_suffix:
GROUP BY p.promo_id
)
SELECT p.promo_id, p.days, COALESCE(d.units, 0) AS promo_units, COALESCE(b.units, 0) AS baseline_units
FROM promo p
LEFT JOIN during d ON d.promo_id = p.promo_id
LEFT JOIN baseline b ON b.promo_id = p.promo_id
